{{Use list-defined references|date=March 2022}}
'''Adriana Irma Pesci''' is an Argentine [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], specialising in [[fluid dynamics]]. Her research topics have included [[Flory–Huggins solution theory|lattice models of polymer solutions]],{{ran|A}} [[Hele-Shaw flow]],{{ran|B}} [[Flagellum|flagellar motion of organisms]] in fluids,{{ran|C}} [[soap films]] on [[Möbius strip]]s,{{r|NYT|twist}}{{ran|D}} and the [[Leidenfrost effect]].{{ran|E}}

==Education and career==
Pesci is originally from Argentina,{{r|kar17}} and earned her Ph.D. in 1986 at the [[National University of La Plata]] in Argentina.{{r|arizona}} She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Chicago]], under the mentorship of [[Leo Kadanoff]] and Norman Lebovitz.{{r|kar17}}

She joined the [[University of Arizona]] as a lecturer in physics in 1999,{{r|arizona}} becoming a senior lecturer in 2003. In 2007 she moved to the [[University of Cambridge]], where she is a senior research associate in the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics,{{r|profile}} a fellow of [[King's College, Cambridge|King's College]],{{r|kcc}} and a former Darley Fellow in Mathematics of [[Downing College, Cambridge|Downing College]].{{r|downing}}

==Personal life==
Pesci married [[Raymond E. Goldstein]], a frequent coauthor who was also a postdoctoral researcher in Chicago and moved with her to Arizona and Cambridge.{{r|where-now}}
